hook: If budgets never stick for you, try the simplest one there is.

blocks.narration: If budgets never stick for you, try the simplest one there is. It only has three numbers: fifty, thirty, and twenty.
blocks.visual: A clay paycheck slides onto a table and splits into three neat colored trays

blocks.narration: Start with your take-home pay. That is the amount that actually lands in your bank account after taxes and other deductions.
blocks.visual: A clay bank card glows as a stream of coins lands in a single bowl

blocks.narration: Fifty percent goes to needs. Rent, groceries, insurance, utilities, and minimum debt payments. Basically, the bills you cannot skip each month.
blocks.visual: The largest tray fills with a tiny house, a grocery bag, and a light bulb

blocks.narration: Thirty percent goes to wants. Eating out, streaming, travel, and hobbies. Yes, fun gets its own budget here, and that is on purpose.
blocks.visual: The middle tray fills with a tiny pizza, a movie ticket, and a suitcase

blocks.narration: Twenty percent goes to your future. That means emergency savings, retirement investing, or paying off debt faster than the minimum.
blocks.visual: The smallest tray fills with a little vault and a growing plant

blocks.narration: On four thousand dollars a month, that is two thousand for needs, twelve hundred for wants, and eight hundred for savings.
blocks.visual: Coins pour into the three trays in matching proportions, settling into place

blocks.narration: If needs eat more than half, that is useful information. It tells you exactly where the pressure in your budget is.
blocks.visual: The needs tray overflows slightly, a small magnifying glass hovering above it

blocks.narration: Treat it as a starting point, not a rule. Try it on this month's paycheck and tell me which bucket surprised you.
blocks.visual: All three trays glow softly as the camera pulls back

cta: Try it on this month's paycheck and tell me which bucket surprised you.

captions.hook_line: The simplest budget that actually works: 50/30/20 🧾
captions.body: Split take-home pay into 50% needs, 30% wants and 20% savings or extra debt payments. On $4,000 a month: $2,000, $1,200 and $800.
